chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Aidh al-Ahmasi, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said:
Zayn al-'Abidin, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, said:

Lo, the most beloved of you to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the best of you in deeds. Indeed, the greatest of you in portion with Allah is the one among you with the strongest desire for what is with Allah. Indeed, the one most saved among people from the punishment of Allah is the one with the greatest fear of Allah. Indeed, the closest of you to Allah is the one with the broadest character. Indeed, the most pleasing of you to Allah is the one most abundant toward his dependents.
Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the most God-conscious of you.

key_terms.أَتْقَاكُمْ: the one with the greatest taqwa, God-consciousness
key_terms.أَحْسَنُكُمْ عَمَلًا: the best of people in righteous action
key_terms.رَغْبَةً: earnest desire for what is with Allah

ai.seo_question: What qualities make a person most beloved and honored by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true worth before Allah is measured by righteous deeds, desire for the reward with Him, fear of Him, noble character, and generosity toward one’s family. It culminates in the Qur'anic principle that the most honored people before Allah are those with the greatest taqwa.
